newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end lower, eye U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end lower, eye U.S. data.

text.p: The Australian share market closed lower on Friday, unchanged from its midsession levels with a cautious tone curbing investor interest ahead of U.S. jobs data due later today.
The All Ordinaries index lost 8.9 points to 2,438.5.
Investors proved reluctant to commit in a day of modest activity with potential for major moves on Wall Street and a Victorian holiday weekend dampening most traders' enthusiasm.
"Most people are just waiting for the U.S. tonight to see where they go," said a dealer at a Sydney brokerage.
With bond yields climbing both in the U.S. and locally, the banks suffered, the sector index losing 1.2 percent on the day.

Sector leader National Australia Bank was hardest hit, losing 2.5 percent to A$15.95 (US$12.60). Commonwealth Bank of Australia spent most of the day in negative territory before staging a late comeback to end in the black, up 11 cents at A$13.06. Brokers suggested traders may have been switching.
"CommBank came back well, while NAB saw plenty of selling so there may have been some switching there," the dealer said.
The action was not all on the downside, though, with an improved assessment of the building materials sector's prospects allowing it to bely the general market mood in active trade.
The building materials index jumped 2.6 percent with Boral Ltd, CSR Ltd and Pioneer International all posting solid gains.
Boral hit a three year high of A$3.91 and closed 13.6 cents higher at A$3.806 in active trade of 8.8 million shares, while CSR added 14 cents to A$4.81 on turnover of 3.3 million shares.
Pioneer shares climbed 14.4 cents to A$4.20 on turnover of 4.2 million shares.
Bakery and milling group, Goodman Fielder, posted a 22 percent higher first half net profit of A$55.8 million, pushing its shares three cents higher to A$1.63.
Enginering group National Consolidated reported a net profit for the 18 months to December 31 of A$3.4 million. Its shares were unchanged at A$0.94.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to eight, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
